_doc: Revert-verify mutants for ticket e3bac7b5 / req f28051a9 (validate schema --shapes-mode names the REASONS behind its warning count on the default text surface). Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py packages/cli/tests/integration/validate-schema-warning-breakdown-e3bac7b5.spec.json after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout (both absolute; the spec is committed with a placeholder so a run never mutates a neighbouring session's worktree — integration-test-revert-verify §A76). Guards enumerated from `git diff -U0` (§A8). EVERY axis asserts PRINTED TEXT (§A66): the data behind the breakdown is already collected inside the command and already shipped by --format json / --format earl, so an axis on the internal structure or on either machine branch would pass on the pre-fix code too. TWO guards of the diff carry NO mutant, and the honest reason (§A118) is that neither has an input on which it defends a legal form: (1) `case "unknown-property"` — that constraint is emitted only under ValidatorOptions.closedWorldMode, and runShapesValidation never passes options at all (measured by reading it), so no live warning can carry it; (2) `if (target === undefined || target === "")` inside the class arm — ShaclLiteValidator's class branch passes `actualValue: obj.value` on every push (:455-465), so the bucket is unreachable today and exists so a future emitter that omits the target is NAMED rather than folded into a real reason. ⛤ No sibling `<base>-verify` harness exists ON PURPOSE: this spec's subject is TypeScript driven by jest, which the driver runs directly through `harness`, and every axis lives in the integration suite — the shell-harness convention does not apply here. Stated so the spec is not read as orphaned (hook-matcher-vs-declared-surface §A19). ⛔ Labels: the three `class` buckets name only the IRI FORM. Two earlier labels claimed resolution and type status and were disproved BY EXECUTION in review — `constraint: "class"` has two origins at the emitter, and the range-mismatch origin resolves its target's type while carrying a path-bearing actualValue. M11 / M12 exist so the retracted wording cannot creep back silently.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/cli/src/commands/validate-schema.ts

M1_presence_test_always_false._note: The ONLY thing the class buckets claim: does the target IRI carry a path segment.

M2_collision_bucket_mislabelled._note: The term-iri-collision arm must not fold into another reason (req 00e8079e keeps its own detail block).

M3_symbolic_bucket_mislabelled._note: A non-obsidian target is a symbolic term IRI; calling it absent loses the distinction the ticket exists for.

M4_default_arm_returns_a_class_reason._note: An emitter with no actualValue (minCount) must bucket by constraint, never as a class reason.

M5_order_not_by_count._note: ⛤ First run of this mutant reddened NOTHING, and the cause was the FIXTURE, not the axis: WB9 then held ten no-path and one symbolic warning, where the count order and the code-point order AGREE, so dropping the count term printed the same block. WB9 now holds ten SYMBOLIC and one no-path, making the two orders opposite (§A111 — 'no distinguishing input' is a property of the fixture).

M6_tiebreak_dropped._note: Without the reason tie-break, equal counts follow arrival order — byte-stability of the block is gone.

M8_breakdown_never_printed._note: The EFFECT mutant (§A97): the whole point of the ticket is the printed block.

M9_printed_outside_the_warning_guard._note: Placement: the block belongs INSIDE `if (warningResults.length > 0)`, so a clean vault stays silent. The hoisted copy is byte-faithful (padStart + its own width) ON PURPOSE — the first draft printed it unpadded, which reddened WB9 as well and made the mutant read as unaddressed (§A43).

M10_totality_class_results_only._note: ORCH-required totality guard: a breakdown that walked only `class` results would still add up on a class-only fixture. ⛤ Predicted [WB4, WB10] and measured [WB4, WB8, WB10]: WB8 also asserts that the collision reason appears as its own bucket, so it is a legitimate third consequence, not axis mixing (§A44). Recorded as measured, not as predicted.
M10_totality_class_results_only.from:
for (const warning of warnings) {
    const reason = classifyWarningReason(warning);
M10_totality_class_results_only.to:
for (const warning of warnings.filter((w) => w.constraint === "class")) {
    const reason = classifyWarningReason(warning);

M11_with_path_label_claims_type_status._note: The retraction itself needs a mutant: the label must not come back as a claim about resolution or type. WB12 and WB13 assert the ABSENCE of the retracted wording, so restoring it reddens exactly them. ⛤ Predicted [WB2, WB4, WB9, WB12, WB13] and MEASURED [WB2, WB12, WB13]; the expectation was over-broad, not an axis gone missing. WB4 asserts bucket COUNT and the sum, neither of which a label rename touches; WB9's fixture carries no with-path warning at all. Recorded as measured (§A44).
M11_with_path_label_claims_type_status.from:
const WARNING_REASON_WITH_PATH =
  "class target IRI has a path segment under obsidian://vault/";
M11_with_path_label_claims_type_status.to:
const WARNING_REASON_WITH_PATH =
  "target resolved in this vault, but carries no resolvable type";

M12_no_path_label_claims_absence._note: Same for the other half: 'not present in this vault' is a presence claim the IRI form does not establish (a vault-ROOT target also has no path segment). ⛤ Predicted [WB1, WB4, WB9, WB13] and MEASURED [WB1, WB8, WB9, WB11, WB13]: WB4 stays green for the same reason as M11, and WB8 / WB11 redden legitimately because both read this label's text.
M12_no_path_label_claims_absence.from:
const WARNING_REASON_NO_PATH =
  "class target IRI has no path segment under obsidian://vault/";
M12_no_path_label_claims_absence.to:
const WARNING_REASON_NO_PATH =
  "target not present in this vault (cross-vault / unmounted assetspace)";
